mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, market expectations for future rate hikes diminish, reducing discounting of future earnings and thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during qualifying periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the mean discount rate on equities does not decrease significantly during the policy window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative during qualifying labor market events (mean p-value > 0.05 across 5 event windows), or the correlation between labor indicators and SPX returns is below 0.2 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months predicts increased near-term economic activity, prompting higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative during qualifying INDPRO acceleration events (mean p-value > 0.05), or the effect size is smaller than one standard error.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in goods orders (RSAFS) of more than 10% in a single month is interpreted as a supply-side shock that reduces growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% in a single month
failure_condition: During qualifying RSAFS contractions, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or the shock is not statistically associated with lower earnings growth forecasts.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 3% for the first time in three months, markets anticipate tighter policy and preemptively discount future cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases and crosses above 3% in a 3-month window
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation breakout periods (p > 0.05), or the discount rate on equities does not rise significantly during the episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a cooling labor market, lowering growth prospects and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >5% in a month while UNRATE rises by >0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during qualifying labor market conditions (mean p-value > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer spending proxies (e.g., retail sales not available, proxy via GDPC1 industrial demand) suggests weakening demand, which reduces earnings growth forecasts and yields negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >4% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during qualifying GDPC1 declines (p > 0.10), or the effect is not robust to alternative demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) turns negative for the first time in a 6-month window, it signals a supply-side weakness that lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, especially in a recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for the first time in 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO declines in recession regimes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by non-supply factors.
